options.label: A
options.completeness: Claims PIT rewrites Java source for each mutant, then names Maven/pitest-maven, repeated recompilation and HTML output; execution and report aspects are present, while the mutation-mechanism claim is false.
options.wrong_defense: Could be defended only if ‘rewrites sources’ referred to a different mutation tool; PIT's documented operators modify compiled bytecode, and project preparation is not per-mutant recompilation.

options.label: B
options.completeness: Covers mutation mechanism, Maven goal and report; details and caveats are in explanatory sections.

options.label: C
options.completeness: Covers mechanism, test preparation, CLI and report; the exclusivity claim is false because PIT also provides pitest-maven.
options.wrong_defense: CLI is a real supported entry point, but the option says it is the only one; official Maven quick start documents the plugin and mutationCoverage goal.

options.label: D
options.completeness: Covers mechanism and Maven use; falsely excludes HTML reporting.
options.wrong_defense: Terminal logs are available, but do not make HTML unavailable; Maven quick start documents an HTML report under target/pit-reports.

sources.checked_claim: PIT applies mutation operators to compiled bytecode; tests run against mutated class.
pitest-maven plugin, mutationCoverage goal, Maven command, HTML report and withHistory are documented.
CLI is supported, requires PIT/dependencies/test framework on classpath, and writes HTML reports; plugins are recommended.
History stores prior run results and infers some unchanged results with dependency assumptions and potential error.
JUnit 5 plugin README states adapter 1.2.3 requires PIT 1.19.4+ and is configured as PIT plugin dependency.
